newsitem.title: ITALY: Tiber dive goes ahead as Italy shivers into 1997.
newsitem.headline: Tiber dive goes ahead as Italy shivers into 1997.

text.p: Three men dived into the River Tiber in Rome to mark the New Year on Wednesday as the rest of Italy saw in 1997 with snow and shivers.
The two Italians and a Moroccan sprinkled the muddy waters of the Tiber with sparkling wine before taking the plunge from the Cavour Bridge, continuing an annual tradition begun in 1946.
Hundreds of onlookers on the bridge, the river's banks and in canoes and rowing boats applauded as the trio, stripped to their swimming trunks, dived in.
The ritual went ahead in mild weather that brought a welcome break for the Italian capital from freezing temperatures that set in just after Christmas.
But there was scant respite for much of northern Italy, where 1997 began to a blanket of fresh snow in Milan, Turin, Genoa and other cities.
At least four people have been killed in weather-related incidents across Italy since the cold snap began.
The port of Genoa was one of the worst affected cities and its airport was closed for much of Tuesday.
Provincial roads remained blocked in several areas and road travel in much of the north remained difficult.
More snow was expected during the day, though forecasters said Thursday would bring higher temperatures and some let-up.
